target.title: fix(diagnostic): avoid model-call stream hot-path object copies
target.body:
Related: #91588
Related: #97211

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where diagnostic model-call event accounting still copies stream chunks and model-call event bases with object rest/spread on hot paths. Issue #91588 includes field evidence that points at V8 dictionary-mode `CopyDataProperties` work around the diagnostic stream byte-accounting path during long-running Gateway workloads.

Scope boundary: This PR only addresses diagnostic model-call stream copy/spread hot paths; it does not close the broader Gateway RSS/OOM tracker or prove a multi-day RSS plateau.

## Why This Change Was Made

The change removes object rest from `responseStreamChunkByteLengthUnchecked()` and conditional object spreads from `baseModelCallEvent()` while keeping the same diagnostic event fields. The stream copy now uses a null-prototype target so an own enumerable `__proto__` stream-chunk field remains a data key instead of interacting with `Object.prototype` behavior.

This PR is ready for review for the narrow diagnostic hot-path mitigation because validation now covers focused regression behavior plus inspectable current-head runtime proof. Longer-running Gateway RSS proof remains outside this submission's current evidence.

## User Impact

Operators running long-lived Gateway sessions should get less diagnostic hot-path object-copy churn during model-call streaming. The change is diagnostic-internal and does not intentionally alter model responses, provider transport, or persisted session data.

## Breaking changes (if any)

None expected.

## Implementation

- Replace `{ partial, ...snapshotlessChunk }` on stream chunks with direct JSON byte accounting for own enumerable fields except `partial`, avoiding a snapshotless chunk allocation on the normal non-`toJSON` path while preserving JSON omission behavior for unsupported values.
- Preserve object-property `JSON.stringify` semantics for non-partial values, including value-level `toJSON(key)` for object/function values and monkey-patched BigInt values, by serializing through a one-property null-prototype wrapper instead of as root values.
- Preserve root `JSON.stringify` semantics when a stream chunk exposes callable `toJSON` via own non-enumerable or inherited/prototype lookup: a rare proxy path hides `partial` lazily, and a descriptor-preserving fallback handles non-configurable/non-extensible shapes.
- Keep own enumerable `__proto__` chunk fields as JSON-serializable data keys without mutating `Object.prototype`, including the `toJSON` snapshot fallback path.
- Build `baseModelCallEvent()` once and assign optional fields conditionally instead of using conditional spread literals.
- Add regression coverage for partial getter safety, value-level `toJSON(key)`, BigInt `toJSON(key)`, callable chunk-level `toJSON`, lazy getter ordering, non-configurable `partial` fallback, and own enumerable `__proto__` data-key preservation.

## Labels considered

`P0`, `impact:session-state`, `impact:message-loss`, `impact:crash-loop`, `clawsweeper:fix-shape-clear`, `clawsweeper:needs-live-repro`, and `clawsweeper:no-new-fix-pr` from #91588 were considered when setting this PR's narrow scope and proof strategy.

## Validation

Current PR head: `7c500070c700e1df312529722553885476da8a73`
Proof baseline commit: `28a841472684eed2d98a1a277fcefc30855b580b`

Current-head GitHub Actions runtime/benchmark proof:

- Latest proof run: `PR 99154 model diagnostic runtime proof` — passed: https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/28677737053
- Latest artifact: `pr99154-model-diagnostic-runtime-proof-28677737053-1` (`summary.md`, `baseline.json`, and `head.json`).
- Environment: GitHub Actions, `ubuntu-24.04`, Node `v24.18.0`, `workflow_dispatch`.
- Head binding: artifact `head.json` records `commit=7c500070c700e1df312529722553885476da8a73`, matching the current PR head. The workflow wrapper branch commit is not used as the proof binding source.
- Supporting repeat run on the same PR head also passed: https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/28677394470 with artifact `pr99154-model-diagnostic-runtime-proof-28677394470-1`.

Latest proof run edge behavior:

- Baseline partial-getter edge failed as expected: expected `34` bytes, actual byte count absent, `partialReads=1`.
- PR head partial-getter edge passed: expected/actual `34` bytes, `partialReads=0`.
- PR head own non-enumerable chunk `toJSON` proxy edge passed: expected/actual `54` bytes, `partialReads=0`, unrelated throwing getter reads `0`.
- PR head inherited/prototype chunk `toJSON` proxy edge passed: expected/actual `35` bytes.
- PR head non-configurable `partial` snapshot fallback edge passed: expected/actual `54` bytes, unrelated throwing getter reads `0`, `objectPrototypeClean=true`.
- PR head own enumerable `__proto__` data-key edge passed: expected/actual `73` bytes, `objectPrototypeClean=true`.
- PR head value-level `toJSON(key)` edge passed: expected/actual `68` bytes, observed key `value`.
- PR head BigInt `toJSON(key)` edge passed: expected/actual `52` bytes, observed key `value`.

Latest proof run synthetic model-call stream benchmark:

- 50,000 representative non-delta stream chunks were drained through `wrapStreamFnWithDiagnosticModelCallEvents()`.
- Baseline and PR head both reported `responseStreamBytes=2911669`, so the diagnostic byte-accounting contract stayed stable.
- Latest run duration: baseline `159.92 ms`, PR head `183.04 ms`; supporting repeat duration: baseline `196.80 ms`, PR head `189.29 ms`. Runtime duration is therefore recorded as short-run signal only, not used as a stable speedup claim.
- Latest run RSS delta: baseline `37,801,984` bytes, PR head `16,318,464` bytes. Short-run RSS deltas are recorded for transparency and are not used as multi-day RSS proof.

Latest proof run large partial-getter benchmark:

- 10,000 chunks with large accumulated `partial` snapshots.
- Baseline `partialReads=10000`; PR head `partialReads=0`.
- Baseline duration `39.88 ms`; PR head duration `39.41 ms`.
- Baseline and PR head both reported expected/actual bytes `527780 / 527780` on the PR head byte-accounting path.

GitHub Actions/check read-back on current PR head:

- Workflow-level current-head rollup completed successfully for the visible PR workflows: `CI`, `CodeQL`, `CodeQL Critical Quality`, `OpenGrep — PR Diff`, `Workflow Sanity`, `iOS Periphery Dead Code`, `Real behavior proof`, `Dependency Guard`, `Security Sensitive Guard`, `Labeler`, `Auto response`, and `ClawSweeper Dispatch`.
- Representative current-head runs:
  - `CI`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28677356289
  - `CodeQL`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28677356252
  - `CodeQL Critical Quality`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28677356260
  - `OpenGrep — PR Diff`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28677356263
  - `Workflow Sanity`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28677356275
  - `Real behavior proof`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28677355555
- Check-run read-back for `7c500070c700e1df312529722553885476da8a73`: `66` success, `29` skipped, `1` neutral, `0` failed, `0` pending.

## Evidence source map

- Issue field evidence: #91588 contains public native stack evidence around V8 `Runtime_CopyDataPropertiesWithExcludedPropertiesOnStack` / dictionary-key collection and identifies the diagnostic stream chunk copy site.
- Current-head GitHub Actions runtime/benchmark proof: https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/28677737053 compares the baseline commit and current PR head with a 50,000-chunk model-call diagnostic stream workload, a 10,000-chunk large-partial getter workload, and edge checks for partial snapshots, value-level `toJSON(key)`, BigInt `toJSON(key)`, callable chunk-level `toJSON`, lazy getter ordering, non-configurable `partial`, and own enumerable `__proto__` data keys.
- Supporting current-head repeat proof: https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/28677394470 passed on the same PR head and independently confirms the edge checks plus 50,000-chunk synthetic stream byte-equivalence.
- Regression tests: `attempt.model-diagnostic-events.test.ts` covers partial snapshot exclusion without reading `partial`, value-level `toJSON(key)`, BigInt `toJSON(key)`, own non-enumerable/prototype chunk `toJSON` behavior, non-configurable `partial` fallback, unrelated lazy getters, and own enumerable `__proto__` data-key byte accounting.
- GitHub Actions/checks: current-head PR workflows completed successfully with no failed or pending check runs in the status rollup.

## Data model / migration compatibility

No persistent data model or runtime storage schema is changed. The modified runtime file constructs transient model-call diagnostic events and diagnostic byte counts; it does not change serialized session-state schemas, vector/embedding metadata, migrations, stores, or upgrade code. The test-file additions exercise in-memory diagnostic event byte accounting only.

## Risk

- Diagnostic byte accounting can be sensitive to unusual provider stream chunk shapes. The added tests and proof cover the relevant review edges: skipping `partial` without reading it, object-property value `toJSON(key)`, BigInt `toJSON(key)`, callable chunk-level `toJSON` lookup/ordering, non-configurable `partial` fallback, and own enumerable `__proto__` data keys.
- The normal non-`toJSON` chunk path remains allocation-conscious: primitive values serialize directly, while object/function values and BigInt values use one small wrapper only when needed to preserve object-property serialization semantics.
- Current-head timing across two short synthetic runs is mixed, so this PR should be evaluated as a focused allocation/read-avoidance and byte-semantics mitigation rather than as broad performance proof.
- This does not address diagnostic maps, session retention, plugin retention, or other long-running RSS contributors discussed in #91588.
- The implementation avoids provider/runtime behavior changes and is limited to diagnostic event construction and byte accounting.

## Rollback

Revert this PR. No data migration, config migration, or persisted format change is involved.

## Docs updated

No documentation files were changed. The patch is limited to diagnostic implementation code plus focused regression tests.

## Related issue / PR

- Related: #91588
- Related: #97211

#97211 covers the same diagnostic hot path and has public review feedback around proof, scope, and `__proto__` behavior. This PR carries focused regression tests and uses non-closing issue references so it does not auto-close the broader Gateway RSS/OOM tracker.

## Review context addressed

- ClawSweeper requested inspectable real behavior proof before merge. The PR body now includes current-head GitHub Actions runtime/benchmark proof and artifact details in Validation.
- ClawSweeper flagged stale proof/head mismatch in the previous review. The latest artifact records `commit=7c500070c700e1df312529722553885476da8a73`, matching the current PR head.
- ClawSweeper flagged persistent data-model compatibility proof as a merge concern. The Data model / migration compatibility section now states the exact persistence boundary: transient diagnostic event construction only, with no serialized session-state, vector/embedding metadata, migration, store, or upgrade-code change.
- Review feedback flagged that the earlier byte counter bypassed callable chunk-level `toJSON` semantics. The implementation now preserves root `JSON.stringify` callable `toJSON` lookup for own non-enumerable and inherited/prototype methods while hiding `partial`.
- Review feedback flagged eager getter reads in the chunk-level `toJSON` snapshot path. The proxy path is lazy, and the fallback copies property descriptors rather than materializing getter values before `JSON.stringify` invokes `toJSON`.
- Review feedback flagged value-level `toJSON(key)` drift for non-partial object properties. The manual byte counter now serializes object/function values through a one-property wrapper so value-level `toJSON` receives the real property key.
- Follow-up static review flagged monkey-patched BigInt `toJSON(key)` as the same object-property semantic edge. The wrapper path now includes BigInt values; ordinary BigInt without `toJSON` still bubbles to the outer catch and skips the byte metric as before.
- The proof compares the baseline commit with the current PR head, verifies partial-snapshot behavior, value-level `toJSON(key)`, BigInt `toJSON(key)`, callable chunk-level `toJSON`, lazy getter ordering, own enumerable `__proto__` data-key behavior, and records synthetic model-call stream and large-partial getter benchmark results.
- The broader #91588 Gateway RSS/OOM scope remains open and non-closing; this PR still only claims the diagnostic model-call stream copy/spread hot-path mitigation.

## Not tested / Limitations

- No multi-day Gateway RSS plateau/soak proof is included here.
- The runtime proof is a GitHub Actions synthetic model-call diagnostic stream benchmark, not a multi-day production Gateway workload.
- Short-run duration and RSS deltas in the proof artifacts are recorded for transparency but are not used as evidence that this PR fixes long-running RSS growth.
- No claim is made that this fixes all memory growth sources in #91588.
